Reproduced: the table header is now 'phase | semantic identity | physical digest | range evidence | shot range | complete' (was 'phase | semantic identity | physical digest | registry digest | shot range | OCI tag'), and grep for 'dd-4.1.1-physical' over the fragment returns 0 hits; the registry digest survives only in the prose line below the table. Cosmetic to the gate, but the spec said 'keeping the rest'; a two-cell addition would have needed no removal.

follow-on: the reviewed run's gate log names the wrong revision on its header line. Reproduced: the header reads 'rev 96a4738dc225be4411268e3928539bff25fa11de tree <worktree> cmd: uv run --no-sync pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/gs/test_description_artifact.py', but the run collected 8 items and the delivered head (9ab5cff3) is what carries 8 tests -- base 96a4738d carries 5. So the log ran the head working tree (post-edit, pre-commit) yet stamped the base sha, which is the revision a reader cannot reproduce the result from. Ties to the same run's manifest, which carries no baseline_suite/after_suite pair: a reader has a single head arm stamped with the base revision and no run-time content sha. The delivered work is sound; the log header is not. Values were correct when measured, and the head gate reproduces green independently (see evidence).

follow-on: _phase_drive_topologies duplicates the load-and-index block of the adjacent _phase_shot_ranges rather than sharing it. Reproduced: both begin with the identical 'if isinstance(machine_map_path, (Path, str)): payload = json.loads(...read_text()) branch, both build a per-row dict from payload['maps'] keyed by row['name']. A single _phase_rows(machine_map_path) helper returning name->row would remove the copy and both missing-phase checks. Harmless (12 lines, same shape), but it is a second parse of one catalogue and the shape the reuse dimension exists to flag.

justifications.durability: One real kept commit, conventional subject with a full body, no AI trailer, tests committed alongside the module, and the landing fragment updated in place rather than a new parallel file. The change is durable against the two defects it repairs (the /home path and the false completeness) because each now has a test: the member-set test, the incompleteness-and-two-gaps test, and the per-phase evidence test. Points off: the reviewed manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite tags, so its base/head state is not machine-readable; the gate log header names the base revision while running the head tree; and the OCI tag the prior record carried is now recorded nowhere in the fragment.

I then ran a second, independent mutation of my own (PHASE_SHOT_EVIDENCE['OP2'] forced to 'observed') and it defeated test_op1_shot_evidence_is_observed_and_op2_inherited on its own (1 failed, 7 passed, EXIT=1), so the added guards are non-vacuous and the recorded red log is real. Ruff whole-tree gate re-run green (All checks passed! EXIT=0). Points off because the reviewed run's own gate log stamps the base revision on a head run (finding 2), so its record does not name the revision its green result came from, and its manifest carries no base/head suite pair.
justifications.fit: Follows section 7 and the plan's own authoring of this repair exactly. Section 7 names the field evidence and the channel drives among the identity inputs, and the plan (jt60sa-machine-map.html:460-479) states the producer carries no channel drives yet, that jtmm-artifact-drive-map later authors the drives, that field evidence stays a named gap so the artifacts remain incomplete, and that the reader already resolves incomplete artifacts. The repair does precisely that: marks complete=False, names both absences, keys the drive-topology name per phase from machine_map.json (jt60sa-pf-drive-op1/-op2, confirmed the machine_map.json values), and passes allow_incomplete=not manifest.complete. Nothing is pushed into nova. The reference producers derive complete from the evidence ledger; this producer now derives it from the evidence it carries, which is the shape section 7's decision rejects-against ('ships an incomplete set as authoritative') now avoided.
justifications.goal_fidelity: All four named changes are implemented and each is verified against the real stores: source paths derived from JT60SA_MAP_DIR with zero '/home/ITER' left in the module; completeness derived per phase with both absences named and complete=False; per-phase shot-range evidence OP1 observed / OP2 inherited; and docstring plus fragment updated so neither claims the whole identity is derived. I authored both phases and read back every value against the fragment's table and the manifest's evidence_inputs -- semantic identities sha256:b58114b4... / sha256:57b347ce..., physical f4ba9a35aab22485 / 08807c77e7b35487, one shared registry 99ac00d8...af110, disjoint ranges 100001-101173 / 101174-999999, both complete=false with the two named gaps, and the member set exactly master.h5 plus the five IDS .h5. Two points off: the fragment's identity table lost the OCI-tag and registry-digest columns where the done-when said 'keeping the rest' (finding 1), and the 'derived' completeness is computed by a helper whose two evidence parameters are never supplied at the call site, so complete is False by construction -- which is what the done-when asked and what the plan's drive-map node later changes, so it is a nominal rather than real derivation for now.
justifications.reuse: Good. It calls the existing read_artifact_* extractors and nova's three generic entries, and the new _phase_completeness is a small pure helper rather than a second manifest builder. One deduction: _phase_drive_topologies copies the load-and-index block of the adjacent _phase_shot_ranges instead of sharing a single _phase_rows helper, so the catalogue is parsed twice through two near-identical functions (finding 3). No parallel reader of the stores, no new module, no widening of a generic entry.
